evidence: WebSearch (allowed_domains sec.gov) returned https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/final/2023/34-99149.pdf ('Conformed to Federal Register version', adopted 2023-12-13, Release 34-99149) and https://www.sec.gov/files/34-99149-fact-sheet.pdf. add_reference.py got HTTP 403 for the PDF.
notes: SEC rate-limit block, same as the T+1 item. Even if reachable, a PDF cannot pass the URL route's HTML title check (see Cboe item). So the likely outcome is not_admissible, not a route-level pass. Not bypassed.

command: tools/add_reference.py --doi 10.1007/978-1-137-52574-1 --source "Kindleberger & Aliber, Manias, Panics, and Crashes, 7th ed. (2015)" --used-by LX1
dry_run_output:
REJECT: record does not match the citation (first_author=False type=book title=1.00 volume_marker=True year=True)
  record: Aliber (2015) 'Manias, Panics, and Crashes: A History of Financial Crises',  None(None)
evidence: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/978-1-137-52574-1 returned title 'Manias, Panics, and Crashes', authors [('Robert Z.', 'Aliber'), ('Charles P.', 'Kindleberger')], issued 2015, Palgrave Macmillan UK. --list-editions also returned Palgrave 2015 listings with no matching edition title.
notes: The record is the right book and year, but Crossref lists Aliber as first author. The citation names Kindleberger first, so the first-author rule rejects it. The citation string may need a human decision about author order; not changed here.

None of these is on an authorities.yaml 'issuers' domain (only case.law, supremecourt.gov are listed for court opinions). A WebSearch limited to case.law returned no results.
notes: No case.law (Caselaw Access Project) page was found, so the allowed route has no URL to fetch. Opinion copies on other hosts are not authoritative under the registry's policy. Adding case.law to authorities.yaml is a policy decision for a human, not made here.
